summary: Homepage news: DHS final rule to end Duration of Status for F students (currently blocked by court).

resolution.note: Homepage blog list rotated, but one post covered the July 2026 DHS final rule that replaces Duration of Status with fixed admission periods. I checked the rule and its status: a D. Mass. preliminary injunction (14 Sep 2026) blocked it, so D/S still applies. Added a caveat to the F-1 D/S paragraph.

edits.oldText: the student can remain in the US as long as their [TERM: sevis|SEVIS] record and [TERM: i-20] are valid.
edits.newText: the student can remain in the US as long as their [TERM: sevis|SEVIS] record and [TERM: i-20] are valid. A DHS final rule published in July 2026 would replace D/S with a fixed admission period (the program length on the I-20, capped at four years, plus 30 days to arrive and 30 days to depart), but a federal court blocked it the day before it was due to take effect on 15 September 2026. For now D/S still applies — check Study in the States for the latest position before you travel.
